summary: This builds a dictionary that maps the name of each shop item to its price in gold. A dictionary stores pairs of keys and values, so you can look up a price by the item's name instead of by a numeric position.

lines.text: Curly braces begin a dictionary literal, and the name `shop` will refer to the finished collection.
The text before the colon is the key and the number after it is the value, so `shop["sword"]` will give back 150.
The final pair needs no trailing comma, and the closing brace on the next line ends the dictionary.
